definition_zh: 执行；强制实施；迫使服从
definition_en: to make people obey a law or rule, often by using authority
core_image: 交警站在路口，确保每辆车都遵守信号灯
scene: 警察负责执行交通规则。The police enforce traffic rules.
sceneCN: 这里 enforce 是「执行」（第 1 个义项：用权威确保人们遵守规则）；句意：警察负责执行交通规则。

senses.title: To make a law or rule obeyed
senses.definition: to make sure that a law or rule is obeyed
senses.definitionCN: 确保法律或规则被遵守
senses.example: The police enforce traffic rules.
senses.exampleCN: 警察负责执行交通规则。
senses.why: The prefix en- adds force, so the word means putting force behind a rule so it is not merely written.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 加上力量，因此这个词意为给规则加力，使它不只是写在纸上。

senses.title: To force people to accept something
senses.definition: to make people accept or follow something by authority or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 通过权威或压力使人们接受或遵守某事
senses.example: The school enforces a strict dress code.
senses.exampleCN: 学校强制执行严格的着装规定。
senses.why: Enforcement can involve pressure, so the word also covers forcing compliance.
senses.whyCN: 执行可能涉及压力，因此这个词也涵盖强迫服从。

senses.title: To give strength to a claim or rule
senses.definition: to make an argument, right, or condition stronger or more effective
senses.definitionCN: 使论点、权利或条件更有力、更有效
senses.example: The new evidence enforces their claim.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据使他们的主张更有力。
senses.why: To enforce is to add force, so a claim can be strengthened as a rule can be upheld.
senses.whyCN: enforce 就是加力，因此主张能像规则一样被加强。

intro.en: Enforce comes from Old French enforcier, to give force to something.
intro.cn: enforce 来自古法语 enforcier，意为给某物加力。

items.en: Fortis means strong, the root behind force.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮，是 force 背后的词根。

items.en: Enforcier means to strengthen or compel.
items.cn: enforcier 意为加强或强迫。

items.en: English borrows enforce with the sense of giving force.

items.en: The legal sense of carrying out laws becomes common.

items.en: Enforce now chiefly means making rules obeyed.
items.cn: 现代英语中，enforce 主要指使规则被遵守。

note.cn: enforce 使规则被遵守，implement 把计划付诸行动，impose 把某物强加于人。

definition_zh: 在……上雕刻；镌刻；使深深铭记
definition_en: to cut a design or letters into a hard surface; to impress something deeply on the mind
core_image: 一枚银戒指的内圈刻着一行极细的字，放大镜下才能看清笔画
scene: 工匠用细针在金属板上刻下客户姓名的首字母。The craftsman used a fine needle to engrave the customer's initials on the metal plate.
sceneCN: 这里 engrave 指「在硬质表面刻字或刻图案」（第 1 个义项：用刀具在金属、石材等表面刻出线条）；句意为工匠用细针在金属板上刻下客户姓名的首字母。图中可辨识物件：金属板、刻针、放大镜、姓名字样。

senses.title: To cut a design into a hard surface
senses.definition: to cut lines or a design into metal, stone, glass or another hard material
senses.definitionCN: 在金属、石材、玻璃等硬质材料上刻出线条或图案
senses.example: The machine engraves a pattern into the steel plate.
senses.exampleCN: 机器在钢板上刻出图案。
senses.why: engrave is en- 'in' plus grave 'to cut', so it literally means to cut a mark into a surface.
senses.whyCN: engrave 是 en-「进入」加 grave「切」，字面意思就是把痕迹刻进表面。

senses.title: To inscribe a name or words on an object
senses.definition: to cut letters or a short text into an object, usually as a record or gift dedication
senses.definitionCN: 把字母或短句刻在物件上，通常用于记录或赠礼题词
senses.example: They engraved her name on the trophy.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把她的名字刻在奖杯上。
senses.why: once the technique was used for words, the verb naturally took a name or a message as its object.
senses.whyCN: 当这项技术用于文字，动词便自然以姓名或词句为宾语。

senses.title: To impress something deeply on the memory
senses.definition: to fix an event or feeling in the mind so firmly that it is not forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 把事件或感受牢牢固定在心中，使其不被遗忘
senses.example: The scene was engraved on his memory for years.
senses.exampleCN: 那一幕在他记忆里刻了许多年。
senses.why: the physical cut became a metaphor for memory because both leave a mark that cannot be smoothed away.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的刻痕成为记忆的比喻，因为两者都留下无法抹平的印记。

senses.title: To prepare a printing plate by cutting
senses.definition: to cut a design into a plate so that it can be inked and printed
senses.definitionCN: 把图案刻入印版，使其能够上墨印刷
senses.example: The artist engraves the copper plate by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术家手工刻制铜版。
senses.why: printing grew out of metalwork, and the plate-maker's verb became the name of an intaglio process.
senses.whyCN: 印刷术源于金属工艺，制版者的动词后来成为凹版工艺的名称。

senses.title: To decorate glass with cut lines
senses.definition: to cut a pattern into glass for decoration, often with a wheel or acid
senses.definitionCN: 用砂轮或酸在玻璃上刻出装饰图案
senses.example: The firm engraves crystal bowls with a leaf pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在水晶碗上刻出叶片图案。
senses.why: glass cutting borrowed the word from metalwork because the action and the tool are nearly the same.
senses.whyCN: 玻璃雕刻从金属工艺借来这个词，因为动作与工具几乎相同。

senses.title: To ornament metal with cut lines
senses.definition: to decorate silver, gold or steel with cut ornamental lines
senses.definitionCN: 在银、金或钢上用刻线作装饰
senses.example: The silversmith engraves the rim with a scrolling border.
senses.exampleCN: 银匠在器口刻出卷草边饰。
senses.why: this is the oldest workshop sense, where engraving is decoration rather than writing or printing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的手工作坊义，此时镌刻是装饰，而非书写或印刷。

senses.title: To make something permanent and unforgettable
senses.titleCN: 使某事固定不变、不可磨灭
senses.definition: to establish a fact or right so firmly that it cannot be removed
senses.definitionCN: 把某项事实或权利确立得如此牢固，以致无法移除
senses.example: The ruling engraved the boundary in law.
senses.exampleCN: 该裁决把这条边界固定在法律中。
senses.why: the figurative sense extends from memory to law, where a fixed mark stands for a fixed rule.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义从记忆扩展到法律，固定的刻痕在那里代表固定的规则。

senses.title: To cut a die or mould for manufacturing
senses.definition: to cut a die, mould or roller used to stamp or shape manufactured parts
senses.definitionCN: 刻制用于冲压或成形工业零件的模具、铸型或辊筒
senses.example: Technicians engrave the roller that prints the wallpaper.
senses.exampleCN: 技师刻制印制壁纸用的辊筒。
senses.why: industrial toolmaking kept the craft verb because the die is still cut line by line.
senses.whyCN: 工业制模保留了这门手艺的动词，因为模具仍是一线一线刻出来的。

intro.en: Engrave is an English formation: the prefix en- 'in' plus grave 'to cut', from Old English grafan. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: engrave 是英语构词：前缀 en-「进入」加 grave「切」，后者来自古英语 grafan。年代均为约数。

items.en: Grafan meant 'to dig, grave, carve', and its family also produced grave 'a trench or tomb'.
items.cn: grafan 意为「挖、刻」，其词族也产生了 grave「沟、坟墓」。

items.en: The verb belongs to a Germanic family of digging and scratching words; the common Germanic shape is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 这个动词属于日耳曼语一族表示「挖、抓」的词；共同日耳曼语形态属于重构，而非有据可查。

items.en: The prefix en- 'in, into', from Latin in- through French, added the idea of cutting a mark into something.
items.cn: 前缀 en-「进入」，经法语来自拉丁 in-，增添「把痕迹刻进去」的意思。

items.en: Engrave is recorded around 1500 with the sense 'to cut into a surface', first of metal and stone.
items.cn: engrave 约在 1500 年有书证，意为「刻入表面」，最初用于金属与石材。

items.en: The printing-plate sense developed in the seventeenth century, and the memory sense followed as a metaphor.
items.cn: 印版义在十七世纪发展起来，记忆义随后作为比喻出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic base of grafan is reconstructed, and its relation to other digging roots is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：grafan 的日耳曼语前词基属于重构形式，它与其他「挖」词根的关系仍有争论。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root family and one word that looks identical to the root but means something else; group two holds other ways of cutting text or images.
note.cn: 第一组是同词根词族，外加一个与词根同形却意义不同的词；第二组是刻写文字或图像的其他方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en（进入）+ grave（刻/墓）」——把字刻进石头 → 雕刻、镌刻

root: 古英语 grafan「挖、刻」→ grave「切」；加前缀 en-「进入」构成 engrave。更早的日耳曼语前词基为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one cut line: into steel, into a trophy, into memory, into a printing plate, into glass, into silver, into law, and into a manufacturing die.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一条刻线展开：刻入钢、刻入奖杯、刻入记忆、刻入印版、刻入玻璃、刻入银器、刻入法律，最后刻入工业模具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp point opening a thin line that cannot be smoothed away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个尖点划开一道细线，再也抹不平。

branches.en: CUTTING SURFACES: metal and glass are marked by the same opening of a line.
branches.cn: 刻入表面：金属与玻璃都靠划开线条留下记号。

branches.en: WRITING AND ORNAMENT: letters on a trophy and scrollwork on silver are both cut decoration.
branches.cn: 文字与装饰：奖杯上的字母与银器上的卷草，都是刻出的装饰。

branches.en: PRINTING AND TOOLS: the plate and the die are cut so that they can reproduce a mark.
branches.cn: 印刷与工具：印版与模具被刻出来，是为了复制记号。

branches.en: MEMORY: a cut in metal stands for a mark that experience leaves in the mind.
branches.cn: 记忆：金属上的刻痕，比喻经验在心上留下的印。

branches.en: PERMANENCE: law borrows the image to say that a rule cannot be removed.
branches.cn: 永久：法律借这个意象表示规则不可移除。

intro.en: Engrave is a Germanic root with a Latin-derived prefix: en- 'in' plus grave 'cut'. The combination is English, not Latin.

definition_en: to hold the whole attention of someone, or in historical use to write the final copy of a document in a large hand, or to buy up land or goods in bulk

scene: 他伏案整夜抄写地契，连送饭来都没听见。The clerk was engrossed in copying the deed all night.

intro.en: Engross is en- plus gross, from Latin grossus, thick; the scribe wrote the final copy in thick large letters, and out of that thickness grew the idea of taking a thing up wholly.
intro.cn: engross 由 en- 加 gross 构成，gross 出自拉丁语 grossus（粗厚）；抄写员用粗大的字体誊写定本，「粗厚」这一层意思又长出了「整个占满」的意象。

items.en: Grossus means thick or bulky in Latin.
items.cn: grossus 在拉丁语中意为粗厚、大块。

items.en: Gros means large, thick or coarse in Old French.
items.cn: 古法语 gros 意为大而厚、粗俗。

items.en: Early English engrossen meant to fatten or make thick.
items.cn: 早期英语 engrossen 指养肥、使变粗厚。

items.en: The verb is used for writing a final legal copy.
items.cn: 15 世纪该动词指誊写法律定本。

items.en: It also comes to mean buying up land or stock in bulk.
items.cn: 该词又指大量购并土地或存货。

items.en: The sense of holding attention completely becomes usual.
items.cn: 18 世纪「完全占据注意力」这一义变得常用。

note.en: Engross, gross and crass all come from Latin grossus, thick; engrossment keeps both the attention sense and the old legal copy sense.
note.cn: engross、gross 与 crass 都出自拉丁语 grossus（粗厚）；engrossment 同时保留注意力义与旧时的法律誊清义。

dict_mnemonic.text: engross ＝ en-（使…）＋ gross（粗大的，拉丁 grossus）＝「写得粗大、填得满满的」。三个用法按历史排列：先指用大字体誊清法律定本，再指大量购并土地货物而独占，最后引申为把注意力全部占满。名词 engrossment 全神贯注与誊清本，同根形容词 gross 总的、粗俗的，crass 愚钝的。常见搭配：engrossed in a book 沉迷于书、engross the market 垄断市场。

definition_zh: 提高；增强；提升价值
definition_en: to improve the quality, strength, or value of something
core_image: 把一件东西一点点垫高，让它在光线下显得更亮、更有分量
scene: 新来的教练没有换掉旧战术，只是把训练强度一点点提上去，球队的速度明显变快。The new coach enhanced the team's speed with small daily drills.
sceneCN: 这里 enhance 是「提高；增强」（第 1 个义项：改善质量或水平）；句意：新教练通过每天的小训练提高了球队的速度。

senses.title: To improve quality
senses.definition: to make something better in quality, usefulness, or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在质量、实用性或外观上变得更好
senses.example: The new windows enhance the look of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 新窗户提升了房子的外观。
senses.why: The word comes from a root meaning high, so enhancing is lifting something to a higher standard.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「高」的词根，所以 enhance 就是把某物提升到更高的水准。

senses.title: To increase strength or degree
senses.definition: to increase the strength, effect, or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 增加某物的强度、效果或数量
senses.example: Regular exercise enhances the body's ability to resist illness.
senses.exampleCN: 规律运动增强身体抵抗疾病的能力。
senses.why: Lifting something higher also means raising its intensity, which gives the sense of strengthening.
senses.whyCN: 把某物抬得更高也意味着提高其强度，于是产生「加强」这一义项。

senses.title: To raise value
senses.definition: to increase the money or social value of something
senses.definitionCN: 提高某物的金钱价值或社会价值
senses.example: The restoration enhanced the value of the old building.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修复提升了这栋老建筑的价值。
senses.why: If quality rises, the price or worth people assign to it can rise too.
senses.whyCN: 如果质量提高，人们赋予它的价格或价值也会随之上升。

intro.en: Enhance comes through Old French enhaucier from Vulgar Latin altiare, to raise, from Latin altus, high.
intro.cn: enhance 经古法语 enhaucier 来自俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高），其根源是拉丁语 altus（高的）。

items.en: Altus means high or deep, and it also gives English altitude.
items.cn: altus 意为高的或深的，也是英语 altitude 的来源。

items.en: Altiare means to make high or raise up.
items.cn: altiare 意为使变高、抬高。

items.en: Old French enhaucier adds en- and means to raise or exalt.
items.cn: 古法语 enhaucier 加上 en-，意为抬高或提升。

items.en: The French verb crosses into English law and courtly writing.
items.cn: 这个法语动词进入英语的法律与宫廷写作。

items.en: Middle English enhance means to raise in rank, value, or dignity.
items.cn: 中古英语 enhance 指提高等级、价值或尊严。

items.en: Modern English widens the word to quality, performance, and effect.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到质量、表现和效果。

note.en: Enhance belongs to a family about making something better or higher, and it sits near words for improving and increasing.
note.cn: enhance 属于「使某物更好或更高」的词族，与改善和增加类词相邻。

normal.en: The en- at the front means make or put into, so enhance is to put something into a higher state.

sensesIntro.en: Lifting something higher gives three results: better quality, greater strength, and higher value.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something lifted to a higher level so that it shows better.

branches.en: Better quality and higher value usually rise together.

examples.en: Two cheap enhancers improved the whole sound system.

dict_mnemonic.text: enhancer ＝ enhance（提高）＋ -er（做这件事的东西）＝「增强器；增强剂」。动词 enhance 经古法语 enhaucier 来自俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高），词根是意为高的 altus。名词 enhancement 是结果，enhancer 是手段。三类用法：设备 a signal enhancer 信号增强器、配料 a flavour enhancer 增味剂、软件 an image enhancer 图像增强器。复数 enhancers 指多种或几件增强装置。

root: 拉丁语 altus（高的）→ 俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高）→ enhance（提高）＋ -er → enhancer（增强器；增强剂）

sensesIntro.en: Three kinds of thing that lift a quality: a box on the desk, a spoon over the pot, a slider on the screen
sensesIntro.cn: 三种把品质抬起来的东西：桌上一个盒子、锅上方的一勺、屏幕上的一个滑块

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one knob turned past the mark until the sound gains air
core.cn: 核心意象：一个旋钮拧过刻度，声音忽然有了空气感

branches.en: Signal and sound get stronger.
branches.cn: 信号与声音变强。

branches.en: Taste and appearance get better.
branches.cn: 味道与外观变好。

branches.en: A picture gains clean edges.
branches.cn: 图像得到清晰的边缘。

branches.en: Both are hardware or software tools.
branches.cn: 两者都是硬件或软件工具。

branches.en: Both add rather than replace.
branches.cn: 两者都是添加而非替换。

intro.en: Enhancer is enhance plus -er; the verb carries en- plus a form of Latin altus, high, and -ment builds the noun of the result.
intro.cn: enhancer 由 enhance 加 -er 构成；动词带 en- 与拉丁语 altus（高）的一个形式，-ment 构成表结果的名词。

latinIntro.en: Vulgar Latin altiare, to make high, is regularized from Latin altus; from it come enhance, exalt and altitude in different routes.
latinIntro.cn: 俗拉丁语 altiare（使高）由拉丁语 altus 规则化而来；enhance、exalt 与 altitude 循不同路径都出自这一支。

definition_zh: 谜；难以理解的人或事物
definition_en: something or someone that is puzzling and hard to explain
core_image: 一封信上写满看不懂的符号，纸角还压着一枚不属于任何国家的邮票
scene: 她从不解释自己为什么每周三消失，办公室的人猜了很久。Her silence remained an enigma to everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 enigma 指难以理解的人（第 1 个义项：谜一般的人）；句意为她的沉默对所有人始终是个谜。

senses.title: A puzzling person
senses.definition: a person whose motives or history cannot be read
senses.definitionCN: 动机或经历无法被读懂的人
senses.example: Her silence remained an enigma to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她的沉默对所有人始终是个谜。
senses.why: People become enigmas when the usual signs, face, tone and habit, stop yielding meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当惯常的符号，表情、语气与习惯，不再给出意义时，人就变成谜。

senses.title: A puzzling event
senses.definition: an occurrence that has no obvious explanation
senses.definitionCN: 没有明显解释的事件
senses.example: The empty boat was an enigma the village never solved.
senses.exampleCN: 那条空船是村子始终没解开的谜。
senses.why: An event becomes an enigma when its cause is missing but its effect is plain.
senses.whyCN: 当原因缺失而结果清楚时，事件就成了谜。

senses.title: A coded message
senses.definition: a text or signal written to be unreadable without a key
senses.definitionCN: 没有密钥便无法读懂的文本或信号
senses.example: The message was an enigma until the key was found.
senses.exampleCN: 在找到密钥之前，这段讯息是个谜。
senses.why: Here the word is technical: the meaning exists, but the route to it is locked.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词是技术性的：意义存在，通往它的路线却被锁住。

senses.title: An unexplained natural thing
senses.definition: a feature of nature whose cause science has not settled
senses.definitionCN: 科学尚未确定成因的自然特征
senses.example: The migration of the birds is still an enigma.
senses.exampleCN: 这些鸟的迁徙仍是一个谜。
senses.why: Nature keeps a store of questions that resist every simple model.
senses.whyCN: 自然保存着一批拒绝任何简单模型的问题。

senses.title: A work hard to interpret
senses.definition: a book, film or painting whose meaning stays open
senses.definitionCN: 意义始终敞着、难以定论的书、影片或画
senses.example: The final chapter is an enigma by design.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一章是刻意留下的谜。
senses.why: Art can use the same lock as a code, but here the missing key is the point.
senses.whyCN: 艺术可以使用与密码相同的锁，但这里缺失的钥匙正是重点。

senses.title: A national puzzle
senses.definition: a public mystery that a whole society discusses
senses.definitionCN: 整个社会都在讨论的公共谜团
senses.example: The vanished ship became a national enigma.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘消失的船成了举国之谜。
senses.why: Scale turns a private puzzle into a shared one, and sharing keeps it alive.
senses.whyCN: 规模把私人的谜变成共同的谜，而共同讨论让它活下来。

senses.title: Enigma as charm
senses.definition: the attractive quality of a person who does not explain everything
senses.definitionCN: 一个不把一切说清的人身上的吸引力
senses.example: He cultivated his enigma as other men cultivate a garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他像别人打理花园那样打理自己的神秘感。
senses.why: Mystery can be a strategy: what is not told keeps other people thinking.
senses.whyCN: 神秘可以是一种策略：没说出的部分让别人一直想着。

senses.title: A riddle of history
senses.definition: an unresolved question about the past that evidence cannot close
senses.definitionCN: 证据无法收束的、关于过去的未解问题
senses.example: Historians still argue over the enigma of the lost colony.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家仍在争论那个消失殖民地的谜。
senses.why: The past leaves gaps that no amount of evidence can fill, and the gap itself becomes a subject.
senses.whyCN: 过去留下的空白，再多证据也填不满，而空白本身成了主题。

intro.en: Enigma is a Greek word for a riddle, and it shares an origin with the word 'guess'.
intro.cn: enigma 是希腊语中表示谜语的词，它与英语的 guess 出自同一来源。

items.en: Greek ainigma meant 'a dark saying, a riddle', something spoken to be decoded.
items.cn: 希腊语 ainigma 意为「隐语、谜语」，是为被解码而说出的东西。

items.en: Ainissesthai 'to speak darkly' is the verb behind it, from a root for tale or story.
items.cn: ainissesthai「隐晦地说」是其背后的动词，词根与故事有关。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as aenigma, keeping both the riddle and the darkness.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 aenigma，把谜语与晦暗都保留下来。

items.en: English took it in the 16c.; by the 17c. it could describe a person as well as a text.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入；到十七世纪它已能形容人，也能形容文本。

items.en: Today it covers ciphers, natural puzzles and anyone whose motives stay closed.
items.cn: 今天它覆盖密码、自然谜题，以及任何动机封闭的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the enigmatic stem; the near-meaning group distinguishes kinds of unexplained things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 enigmatic 词干；近义组区分不同种类的未解之物。

entries.definition: mysterious and hard to interpret
in a way that is hard to understand
to turn something into a puzzle
a question posed as a puzzle to be solved.
entries.definitionCN: 作为待解谜题提出的问题。

entries.definition: something unknown or unexplained.
a problem that confuses the mind.
a secret way of writing or a text in it.
entries.definitionCN: 秘密写法或以此写成的文本。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a letter full of symbols that no one in the room can read.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一封信写满符号、屋里没人读得懂」的画面。

normal.en: Enigma hides a name: the Enigma machine was the coded puzzle of the war.
normal.cn: enigma 藏着一个名字：Enigma 密码机就是那场战争中的谜。

normal.en: Say ih-NIG-muh; the short i sounds like a locked door.
normal.cn: 读成 ih-NIG-muh，短促的 i 像一扇锁住的门。

normal.en: Link with guess: both come from the same old root for telling a tale.
normal.cn: 和 guess 联系：两者都出自同一个表示「讲故事」的古词根。

normal.en: Think of a box with no lid and no visible seam.
normal.cn: 想象一个没有盖子、也看不到接缝的盒子。

normal.en: Enigma ends in -ma, like drama: a mystery is something staged for others to watch.
normal.cn: enigma 以 -ma 结尾，像 drama：谜是被摆出来给人看的戏。

abstract.en: A code and a person can be equally unreadable; the word does not care which.
abstract.cn: 密码和人可以同样难读；这个词不在乎是哪一个。

abstract.en: Mystery is not ignorance; it is knowledge that something is deliberately withheld.
abstract.cn: 神秘不是无知；它是知道有东西被刻意扣住。

abstract.en: What resists explanation longest often attracts the most attention.
abstract.cn: 最久拒绝解释的东西，往往吸引最多注意。

examples.en: Her silence remained an enigma to everyone.
examples.cn: 她的沉默对所有人始终是个谜。

examples.en: The empty boat was an enigma the village never solved.
examples.cn: 那条空船是村子始终没解开的谜。

examples.en: The migration of the birds is still an enigma.
examples.cn: 这些鸟的迁徙仍是一个谜。

dict_mnemonic.text: e（出）+ nig（暗）+ ma（名词）：从暗处说出的东西，就是「谜」。

root: 希腊语 ainigma（谜语），源自 ainissesthai（隐晦地说）

sensesIntro.en: An enigma is a meaning that exists but will not come out; the senses differ in what is holding the door shut.
sensesIntro.cn: enigma 是一个存在却不肯出来的意义；各义项的差别在于谁把门关着。

core.en: A MEANING THAT WILL NOT COME OUT
core.cn: 不肯出来的意义

branches.en: A person whose motives stay closed, and the charm that follows.
branches.cn: 动机封闭的人，以及随之而来的魅力。

branches.en: Events and public puzzles that a whole society discusses.
branches.cn: 整个社会讨论的事件与公共谜团。

branches.en: Coded text that needs a key.
branches.cn: 需要钥匙的密码文本。

branches.en: Nature and history keeping questions open.
branches.cn: 自然与历史保持开放的问题。

branches.en: Art that leaves the key missing on purpose.
branches.cn: 故意让钥匙缺失的艺术。

intro.en: The enigm family keeps the same lock: a noun for the puzzle, an adjective for its manner and an adverb for how it is done.
intro.cn: enigm 词族守着同一把锁：名词指谜，形容词指其气质，副词指其做法。

latinIntro.en: Greek ainigma came through Latin aenigma; the spelling settled on en-, but the darkness stayed.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 ainigma 经拉丁语 aenigma 传来；拼写落定为 en-，而晦暗留了下来。

items.meaning: of the nature of a riddle

items.example: The old enigmata were never solved.
items.exampleCN: 那些古老的谜从未被解开。

items.meaning: a question with a hidden answer

items.example: The cipher used a shifting key.
items.exampleCN: 这套密码使用移位密钥。

definition_zh: 令人愉快的；有乐趣的
definition_en: giving pleasure and making you feel happy
core_image: 一场让人从头笑到尾的聚会，散场时大家还在门口聊天
scene: 周末的午后，一群孩子在草地上追着风筝跑，笑声不断。It was an enjoyable afternoon for everyone in the park.
sceneCN: 这里 enjoyable 是「令人愉快的」（第 1 个义项：能带来快乐的）；句意：对公园里的每个人来说，这都是一个愉快的下午。

senses.title: Giving pleasure
senses.definition: making you feel happy and interested
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到快乐并投入其中
senses.example: It was an enjoyable evening with old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个和老朋友共度的愉快夜晚。
senses.why: The -able ending means able to give, so enjoyable describes something that gives enjoyment.
senses.whyCN: -able 词尾表示「能够给予」，所以 enjoyable 描述「能带来享受的事物」。

senses.title: Pleasant rather than exciting
senses.definition: pleasant and easy to like, without being very intense
senses.definitionCN: 令人舒服、容易喜欢，但不算特别激烈
senses.example: The book is enjoyable but not very deep.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书读起来轻松愉快，但不算深刻。
senses.why: Enjoyment can be quiet as well as intense, so the adjective covers mild pleasantness too.
senses.whyCN: 享受可以安静也可以强烈，所以这个形容词也涵盖温和的愉悦。

intro.en: Enjoyable is enjoy plus the ending -able, meaning able to give enjoyment.
intro.cn: enjoyable 是 enjoy 加词尾 -able，意为「能够带来享受的」。

items.en: Gaudere means to rejoice and lies behind the joy in enjoy.
items.cn: gaudere 意为欢欣，是 enjoy 中 joy 的来源。

items.en: Enjoir means to take pleasure in something.
items.cn: enjoir 意为从某物中获得快乐。

items.en: Middle English enjoy names the act of taking pleasure.
items.cn: 中古英语 enjoy 指获得快乐的动作。

items.en: English adds -able to form enjoyable, able to give pleasure.
items.cn: 英语加 -able 构成 enjoyable，意为「能带来快乐的」。

items.en: The word spreads in reviews and travel writing as a mild praise.
items.cn: 这个词在评论和游记中传播，用作温和的赞美。

items.en: Modern English uses it for experiences that are pleasant and satisfying.
items.cn: 现代英语用它描述愉快而令人满足的经历。

note.en: Enjoyable is the adjective of enjoy, and it sits near pleasant and entertaining words without their stronger claims.
note.cn: enjoyable 是 enjoy 的形容词，与 pleasant、entertaining 等词相邻，但语气更温和。

entries.definition: to take pleasure in something
the pleasure taken in something
in a way that gives pleasure
giving a mild feeling of pleasure
very pleasant indeed
enjoyable and amusing
interesting and amusing to watch or read

normalIntro.en: Enjoyable is just enjoy plus -able, so anything that can be enjoyed is enjoyable.
normalIntro.cn: enjoyable 就是 enjoy 加 -able，所以任何能被享受的东西都是 enjoyable。

normal.en: Take enjoy, add -able: able to give joy.
normal.cn: 取 enjoy 加 -able：能够带来快乐。

normal.en: An enjoyable experience is one you would gladly repeat.
normal.cn: an enjoyable experience 是一段你愿意再经历一次的经历。

normal.en: The ending -ably turns it into the adverb enjoyably.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ably 把它变成副词 enjoyably。

normal.en: Compare enjoyable and delighted: one gives pleasure, one feels it.
normal.cn: 对比 enjoyable 与 delighted：一个给予快乐，一个感受快乐。

normal.en: Highly enjoyable is a common way to praise a book or show.
normal.cn: highly enjoyable 是赞美书或演出的常用说法。

abstract.en: Picture a picnic where nobody wants to pack up.
abstract.cn: 想象一次野餐，谁也不想收拾离开。

abstract.en: Imagine a film that makes the whole row laugh at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一部让整排观众同时发笑的电影。

abstract.en: Think of a walk with no destination but good company.
abstract.cn: 想象一次没有目的地、只有好同伴的散步。

examples.en: We had an enjoyable afternoon by the lake.
examples.cn: 我们在湖边度过了一个愉快的下午。

examples.en: The class is both enjoyable and useful.
examples.cn: 这门课既有趣又有用。

examples.en: She found the work surprisingly enjoyable.
examples.cn: 她发现这份工作出乎意料地令人愉快。

dict_mnemonic.text: enjoy（享受）+ -able（能……的）＝能带来享受的，即令人愉快的；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: enjoy（享受，源自拉丁语 gaudere「欢欣」）+ 形容词词尾 -able，表示「能够带来快乐的」。

sensesIntro.en: Something that gives pleasure is the basic sense, and milder pleasantness is its quieter extension.
sensesIntro.cn: 能带来快乐是基本义，而较温和的愉悦是它更安静的延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an experience people would happily repeat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段人们愿意再来一次的经历。

branches.en: Giving pleasure is the direct meaning of the -able form.
branches.cn: 带来快乐，是 -able 形式的直接含义。

branches.en: Mild pleasantness is a quieter degree of the same pleasure.
branches.cn: 温和的愉悦，是同样快乐中更轻的程度。

branches.en: Both strong fun and quiet comfort count as enjoyable.
branches.cn: 热闹的乐趣与安静的舒适都算 enjoyable。

branches.en: The adjective describes the experience, not the person feeling it.
branches.cn: 这个形容词描述经历本身，而不是感受它的人。

branches.en: It often appears as modest praise rather than high excitement.
branches.cn: 它常作为温和赞美出现，而不是高度兴奋。

intro.en: Enjoyable is a transparent English adjective: enjoy plus -able.
intro.cn: enjoyable 是构词透明的英语形容词：enjoy 加 -able。

latinIntro.en: The base enjoy goes back to Latin gaudere, to rejoice, and -able means able to give.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 enjoy 可上溯到拉丁语 gaudere（欢欣），-able 表示「能够给予」。

items.example: Enjoy is the base of enjoyable.
items.exampleCN: enjoy 是 enjoyable 的基础词。
enjoyable 由 enjoy 与 -able 合成。
enjoyment 共享 enjoy 词干。

items.example: Gaudere is the distant root of enjoy.
items.exampleCN: gaudere 是 enjoy 的远源。

items.example: En- opens the base verb enjoy.
items.exampleCN: en- 出现在基础动词 enjoy 开头。

definition_zh: 扩大；放大；详述
definition_en: to make something bigger, or to speak or write about something in more detail
core_image: 一张小照片被放进放大机，墙上慢慢出现一个更大的影像
scene: 底片洗出来后，她把那张合影放大，挂在客厅的墙上。They enlarged the photo and hung it above the sofa.
sceneCN: 这里 enlarge 是「放大」（第 1 个义项：使尺寸变大）；句意：他们把照片放大后挂在了沙发上方。

senses.title: To make bigger
senses.definition: to make something larger in size or amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在尺寸或数量上变大
senses.example: They enlarged the kitchen by knocking down a wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拆掉一堵墙，把厨房扩大了。
senses.why: The word is en- plus large, so the literal sense is to put something into a large state.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 en- 加 large，字面义就是使某物进入「大」的状态。

senses.title: To become bigger
senses.definition: to grow larger without an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 在没有外部施动者的情况下变大
senses.example: The shadow enlarged as the sun went down.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳落下时，影子变大了。
senses.why: The same size change is seen from the thing's own side, so the verb becomes intransitive.
senses.whyCN: 同样的尺寸变化从事物自身角度看，动词就变成不及物用法。

senses.title: To explain in more detail
senses.definition: to speak or write more about a subject, especially in the phrase enlarge on
senses.definitionCN: 就某主题说得或写得更多，尤用于短语 enlarge on
senses.example: She enlarged on the reasons for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她详细说明了延误的原因。
senses.why: Making an idea bigger by adding detail is a metaphorical extension of making an object bigger.
senses.whyCN: 通过补充细节把想法「变大」，是「把物件变大」的隐喻延伸。

intro.en: Enlarge comes through Old French enlargier from en- plus large, with large going back to Latin largus, abundant.
intro.cn: enlarge 经古法语 enlargier 来自 en- 加 large，而 large 上溯到拉丁语 largus（丰富的、宽大的）。

items.en: Largus means abundant, generous, or wide.
items.cn: largus 意为丰富的、慷慨的或宽大的。

items.en: Large means wide or generous, and enlargier means to make wider.
items.cn: large 意为宽大的或慷慨的，enlargier 意为使变宽。

items.en: The verb passes into English legal language for extending rights or property.
items.cn: 这个动词进入英语法律语言，指扩展权利或地产。

items.en: Middle English enlarge means to increase size, scope, or freedom.
items.cn: 中古英语 enlarge 指增加尺寸、范围或自由。

items.en: Enlarge on develops the sense of adding detail to a subject.
items.cn: enlarge on 发展出「对主题补充细节」的义项。

items.en: Modern English uses it for images, text, rooms, and explanations.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表示放大图像、文字、房间和详细解释。

note.en: Enlarge is the size word of the large family, and it sits near verbs for expanding and magnifying.
note.cn: enlarge 是 large 词族中表示尺寸的词，与扩大和放大类动词相邻。

entries.definition: big in size or extent
mostly, or to a great extent
the act of making something bigger
to become or make larger in size or scope
to make something appear larger
to make something stronger or fuller
to make something wider or more general

normalIntro.en: Enlarge is en- plus large, and en- means make, so the word literally says make large.
normalIntro.cn: enlarge 是 en- 加 large，en- 表示「使」，所以这个词字面上就是「使变大」。

normal.en: En- means make, and large means big: make big.
normal.cn: en- 表示使，large 表示大：使变大。

normal.en: Enlarge a photo is the everyday use of the word.
normal.cn: enlarge a photo 是这个词的日常用法。

normal.en: Enlarge on a point means make the explanation bigger with detail.
normal.cn: enlarge on a point 意为用细节把解释「变大」。

normal.en: Compare large and enlarge: the adjective describes, the verb changes.
normal.cn: 对比 large 与 enlarge：形容词描述，动词改变。

normal.en: The ending -ment makes enlargement, the act or result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ment 构成 enlargement，表示动作或结果。

abstract.en: Picture a photo slowly growing on the wall under an enlarger.
abstract.cn: 想象照片在放大机下慢慢爬满墙面。

abstract.en: Imagine a room opening up when a wall comes down.
abstract.cn: 想象拆掉一堵墙后房间豁然开阔。

abstract.en: Think of a speaker adding one more example to make a point clearer.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者再补一个例子，把观点说得更清楚。

examples.en: Could you enlarge this picture for the exhibition?
examples.cn: 你能把这张照片放大用于展览吗？

examples.en: The company plans to enlarge its factory next year.
examples.cn: 公司计划明年扩建工厂。

examples.en: He enlarged on the plan at the end of the meeting.
examples.cn: 会议结束时他详细阐述了这项计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: en-（使）+ large（大）＝使变大，即扩大、放大；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: en-（使）+ large（大的，源自拉丁语 largus「宽大的、丰富的」）→ 古法语 enlargier → 中古英语 enlarge。

sensesIntro.en: Making something larger comes first, then growing larger by itself, and finally making an explanation larger with detail.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是把某物变大，再是自身变大，最后是用细节把解释「变大」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small image or space opening into a larger one.
core.cn: 核心意象：小小的影像或空间展开成更大的样子。

branches.en: Making something bigger is the literal transitive sense.
branches.cn: 使某物变大，是字面的及物义项。

branches.en: Becoming bigger is the same change seen from the object.
branches.cn: 自身变大，是从对象角度看的同一变化。

branches.en: Adding detail makes an idea bigger in explanation.
branches.cn: 补充细节，使解释中的想法「变大」。

branches.en: Both transitive and intransitive uses describe one size change.
branches.cn: 及物与不及物用法都描述同一次尺寸变化。

branches.en: Physical growth and expanded explanation both add extent.
branches.cn: 物理增长与解释扩展都增加「范围」。

intro.en: Enlarge is a French-shaped verb made from a prefix and the adjective large.
intro.cn: enlarge 是由前缀与形容词 large 构成的法语形态动词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix en- means to make, and large goes back to Latin largus, abundant or wide.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 en- 表示使，large 上溯到拉丁语 largus（丰富的、宽大的）。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 enlarge 与 enable 开头。

items.example: Large is the base of enlarge.

items.example: Largus is the distant source of large.
items.exampleCN: largus 是 large 的远源。

items.example: Enlargier brings the verb into English.
items.exampleCN: enlargier 把这个动词带入英语。
enlarge 由 en- 与 large 合成。

scene: 讲座最后一问，把讲者也一并点醒。That single question enlightened the whole lecture hall.

senses.title: To give understanding
senses.definition: to give someone new understanding of something
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把新的理解交给某人

intro.en: Enlighten is en- plus light, from Old English leoht; the prefix turns the noun into a verb of putting, so to enlighten is literally to put light into a mind.
intro.cn: enlighten 由 en- 加 light 构成，light 来自古英语 leoht；前缀把名词变成一个表示放入的动词，所以 enlighten 的本义就是把光放进一个头脑里。

items.en: Leoht is the Old English noun for light.
items.cn: 古英语 leoht 是表示光的名词。

items.en: The verb leohtan means to make bright.
items.cn: 古英语动词 leohtan 意为照亮。

items.en: Inlighten appears with a religious sense of illumination.
items.cn: 13 世纪 inlighten 出现，带宗教色彩的照亮之义。

items.en: The spelling with en- becomes the standard form.
items.cn: 16 世纪带 en- 的拼法成为标准形式。

items.en: The noun names an age of reason and free thought.
items.cn: 18 世纪该名词指理性与自由思想的启蒙时代。

items.en: Guides and manuals use the verb for plain explanation.
items.cn: 20 世纪手册与指南用这个动词表示日常层面的讲解。

note.en: Enlighten and light share the Old English noun for brightness; illuminate and edify carry the same idea from Latin roots, while en- here turns a noun into a verb of giving.
note.cn: enlighten 与 light 共用古英语中表示光亮的名词；illuminate 与 edify 从拉丁词根表达同一层意思，而这里的 en- 把名词变成表示给予的动词。

entries.definition: the state of a mind free from ignorance
brightness that lets things be seen
to come down from a horse or a vehicle
to supply light or understanding to something
to instruct someone so that thinking develops
to make something clear by explaining it

normalIntro.en: En plus light: to put light into a mind

normal.en: Light is a native noun; en- is a borrowed prefix

normal.en: Enlightenment names the result, enlighten names the act

examples.cn: 讲解员停顿了一下，随后向众人说明了这座桥的建造年代。

examples.en: She wanted a book that would enlighten without preaching.
examples.cn: 她想要一本只有启发、不带说教的书。

examples.en: The audit read less as an accusation than as an enlightenment.
examples.cn: 这次审计与其说是指控，不如说是一次开蒙。

dict_mnemonic.text: enlighten ＝ en-（使…进入）＋ light（光）＝「照亮；启发」。词根是古英语 leoht（光），13 世纪先有 inlighten，16 世纪换成带 en- 的拼写。名词 enlightenment 一义指个人的顿悟，一义特指 18 世纪的启蒙时代。三条使用线：启发某个人、开导一群人、纠正一个误解。口语短语 could you enlighten me 表面客气，常含讽刺。

root: 古英语 leoht（光）→ 古英语 leohtan（照亮）→ 13 世纪 inlighten → en- ＋ light → enlighten（使有光；启发）

sensesIntro.en: Three acts of giving light: a match in a dark room, a shutter at dawn, one eyebrow over an unexplained bill
sensesIntro.cn: 三种给光的动作：暗室里的一根火柴、清晨推开的一扇百叶窗、一张说不清的收据上方的一只挑眉

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one match struck in a dark room until the map on the wall can be read
core.cn: 核心意象：暗室里划亮一根火柴，直到墙上的地图看得懂

branches.en: Light reaches one dark room.
branches.cn: 光照进一间暗室。

branches.en: Light reaches a whole street.
branches.cn: 光照到一整条街。

branches.en: Light reaches one mistaken idea.
branches.cn: 光照进一个错误的想法。

branches.en: Both widen what a mind can see.
branches.cn: 两者都扩大一个头脑所能看见的范围。

branches.en: Both arrive as a sudden answer.
branches.cn: 两者都像一个忽然给出的答案那样到来。

intro.en: Enlighten is en- plus light; en- adds the sense of putting something into, and the noun ending -ment builds enlightenment.
intro.cn: enlighten 由 en- 加 light 构成；en- 增加把某物放入的意思，名词词尾 -ment 构成 enlightenment。

latinIntro.en: The stem is not Latin but Old English leoht; the prefix en- is French, so this is a native word dressed in a borrowed prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的 stem 不是拉丁语而是古英语 leoht；前缀 en- 来自法语，所以这是本族词根配上一个借来的前缀。

definition_zh: vt. 征募；使入伍；争取支持 / vi. 参军；应募
definition_en: to enter the armed forces or to put someone into them, and more broadly to obtain help or support for a task
core_image: 招募处的木桌前排到街角，职员在格线本上一行行写下去
scene: 招募处的木桌前排到街角，职员在格线本上一行行写下去。The recruiter enlisted forty volunteers in a single week.
sceneCN: 这里 enlisted 指「征募；使入伍」（第 1 个义项：把名字写进名册）；句意是一周之内招募处就登记了四十名志愿者。

pos.zh: 征募；使入伍；争取（帮助或支持）

enlist someone to count the boxes

senses.title: To enter armed service
senses.definition: to join the armed forces, or to put someone into them
senses.definitionCN: （动词）加入武装力量，或使某人加入其中
senses.example: The recruiter enlisted forty volunteers in a single week.
senses.exampleCN: 招募官一周之内就登记了四十名志愿者。
senses.why: A name written on a ruled line, with age and height added after it
senses.whyCN: 一条格线上写下姓名，后面补上年龄与身高

senses.title: To get help for a task
senses.definition: to obtain help or support from people for a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: （动词）为某项工作从别人那里取得帮助或支持
senses.example: She enlisted two neighbours to move the piano.
senses.exampleCN: 她请动两位邻居一起搬那架钢琴。
senses.why: Two pairs of hands appearing where one pair was expected
senses.whyCN: 本来只备了一双手，却出现两双手

senses.title: To secure an advantage
senses.definition: to secure something as an advantage for a cause
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把某种东西变成一项事业的优势
senses.example: The speech enlisted the anger of the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 那场演说把人群的怒气变成了自己的力量。
senses.why: A raised hand spreading row by row through a hall
senses.whyCN: 一只手举起，随后一排排传遍整个大厅

intro.en: Enlist is en- plus list. List once meant a strip or border, then a strip of paper with names written in rows, so to enlist is to put a name onto that paper.
intro.cn: enlist 由 en- 加 list 构成。list 最初指窄条或边缘，后指写满一行行名字的窄纸条，所以 enlist 就是把名字写到那张纸上。

items.en: Liste is a strip or band of paper or cloth.
items.cn: 古英语 liste 指一条纸带或布带。

items.en: Medieval Latin lista keeps the sense of a narrow strip.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 lista 保留窄条之义。

items.en: List comes to mean a roll of names.
items.cn: 14 世纪 list 引申为登记名册。

items.en: Enlist appears for writing a name on a roll.
items.cn: 16 世纪 enlist 出现，指把名字登记入册。

items.en: The verb narrows to service in army and navy.
items.cn: 17 世纪词义收窄到陆海军服役。

items.en: General use covers help, support and sympathy.
items.cn: 20 世纪通用义扩展到帮助、支持与同情。

note.en: Enlist keeps the paper sense of list; enroll writes a name on a record too, while recruit and conscript name the military act from other roots.
note.cn: enlist 保留了 list 的纸张本义；enroll 同样把名字写进记录，而 recruit 与 conscript 从别的词根指称征兵这一行为。

entries.definition: a set of names written in rows
the act of joining the armed forces
to put a name on an official record
to take new people into an organisation
to enlist people by law
to prepare people and supplies for action

normalIntro.en: En plus list: to put a name onto the roll
normalIntro.cn: en- 加 list：把名字写到名册上

normal.en: Lista was a narrow strip of paper before it was a roll

normal.en: A desk in line, two pairs of hands, one raised in a hall

normal.en: The army sense takes in, the everyday sense takes help

normal.en: The noun enlistment records the act, the person is the enlistee
normal.cn: 名词 enlistment 记录这件事，被登记的人则是 enlistee

abstract.en: A name written on a ruled line, with age and height added after it
abstract.cn: 一条格线上写下姓名，后面补上年龄与身高

abstract.cn: 本来只备了一双手，却出现两双手

abstract.en: A raised hand spreading row by row through a hall

examples.en: He enlisted at nineteen and came back an officer.
examples.cn: 他十九岁应征入伍，回来时已是军官。

examples.en: The committee enlisted two retired teachers to check the files.
examples.cn: 委员会请动两位退休教师来核对档案。

examples.en: Nobody enlisted the volunteers for the night shift.
examples.cn: 没有人替夜班争取到志愿者。

dict_mnemonic.text: enlist ＝ en-（使…进入）＋ list（名单）＝「登记入册；征募」。list 的本义是窄条、纸带，14 世纪变成写满名字的名册，16 世纪加上 en- 成为动词，17 世纪专指陆海军。名词 enlistment 指登记这件事，enlistee 指被登记的人。三条线：enlist in 参军、enlist help 争取帮助、enlist sympathy 博得同情。军事语境常用被动 be enlisted。

root: en-（使…进入）＋ list（名单，原指窄条、纸带）→ enlist（登记入册；征募）

sensesIntro.en: Three scenes of writing a name down: a desk in a queue, two pairs of hands, one hand raised in a hall
sensesIntro.cn: 三种写下名字的场景：排队尽头的桌子、两双手、大厅里举起的一只手

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clerk filling one ruled line after another at a recruiting desk
core.cn: 核心意象：招募桌前的职员在格线上一行接一行地填写

branches.en: A name enters the military roll.
branches.cn: 一个名字进入军队名册。

branches.en: A name enters a task list.
branches.cn: 一个名字进入工作清单。

branches.en: A feeling is gathered like a name.
branches.cn: 一种情绪被像名字一样收集起来。

branches.cn: 两者都始于在纸上书写。

branches.en: Both ask other people to appear.
branches.cn: 两者都需要别人到场。

definition_zh: 巨大的；庞大的；极大的
definition_en: extremely large in size, amount, or degree
core_image: 一头鲸从船边浮起，船在它旁边像一片叶子
scene: 博物馆大厅中央立着一具恐龙骨架，参观者站在下面显得很小。The skeleton was enormous, filling the whole hall.
sceneCN: 这里 enormous 是「巨大的」（第 1 个义项：尺寸极大）；句意：这具骨架极其巨大，占满了整个大厅。

senses.title: Extremely large in size
senses.definition: much bigger than usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 比通常或预期大得多
senses.example: An enormous tree stood in the middle of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 花园中央立着一棵巨大的树。
senses.why: The Latin source means outside the rule, and something outside normal measure is first of all huge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「超出常规」，而超出常规尺度的东西首先就是巨大的。

senses.title: Extremely great in degree
senses.definition: very great in amount, power, or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、力量或重要性上极大
senses.example: The project required an enormous amount of work.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目需要极大的工作量。
senses.why: The same sense of exceeding normal limits applies to abstract quantities such as effort and pressure.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「超出正常限度」也适用于努力、压力等抽象数量。

senses.title: Outrageous or monstrous
senses.definition: shockingly bad or wicked, an older literary sense
senses.definitionCN: 令人震惊地坏或邪恶，较古老的文学义项
senses.example: The poem describes an enormous crime against the innocent.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗描述了一桩针对无辜者的骇人罪行。
senses.why: Something outside the rule of right conduct was originally called enormous before the word shifted to size.
senses.whyCN: 超出正当行为之「常规」的事，原本就被称作 enormous，后来词义才转向尺寸。

intro.en: Enormous comes from Latin enormis, outside the rule, from e-, out of, and norma, a rule or square.
intro.cn: enormous 来自拉丁语 enormis（超出常规），由 e-（出于）与 norma（规则、曲尺）构成。

items.en: Norma means a carpenter's square and then any rule or standard.
items.cn: norma 指木匠的曲尺，后来泛指规则或标准。

items.en: Enormis means out of rule, irregular, and therefore monstrous or shocking.
items.cn: enormis 意为不合规则的、异常的，因此有「骇人」之意。

items.en: Old French enorme keeps the sense of something shocking and excessive.
items.cn: 古法语 enorme 保留「骇人、过度」的意思。

items.en: Middle English enormous describes both wicked acts and great size.
items.cn: 中古英语 enormous 既描述邪恶行为，也描述巨大尺寸。

items.en: The size sense becomes dominant in ordinary usage.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，尺寸义在日常用法中占据主导。

items.en: Modern English uses enormous mainly for very great size or amount.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用 enormous 表示极大的尺寸或数量。

note.en: Enormous belongs to the norm family, and it sits near adjectives for very great size.
note.cn: enormous 属于「常规」词族，与表示极大尺寸的形容词相邻。

entries.definition: to a very great degree
great size, or a serious wrong
a standard or usual pattern
very large
extremely large
extremely wide or great in area
very large, heavy, and solid

normalIntro.en: Enormous contains norm, so the memory hook is something so big that it is outside the normal measure.
normalIntro.cn: enormous 含有 norm，记忆钩子是「大到超出了正常尺度」。

normal.en: E- means out of, and norm means rule: outside the rule, therefore huge.
normal.cn: e- 表示出于，norm 表示规则：超出规则，所以巨大。

normal.en: Enormous amount is the most common abstract collocation.
normal.cn: enormous amount 是最常见的抽象搭配。

normal.en: The ending -ly gives enormously, meaning very much.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 构成 enormously，意为「极大地」。

normal.en: Compare huge and enormous: enormous often adds a sense of excess.
normal.cn: 对比 huge 与 enormous：enormous 常多一层「过度」的意味。

normal.en: The noun enormity can mean great seriousness as well as great size.
normal.cn: 名词 enormity 既可指巨大，也可指严重性。

abstract.en: Picture a whale surfacing beside a small boat.
abstract.cn: 想象一头鲸在小船旁浮出水面。

abstract.en: Imagine standing under a dinosaur skeleton that fills a hall.
abstract.cn: 想象站在占满大厅的恐龙骨架下面。

abstract.en: Think of a shadow so long it reaches across a whole street.
abstract.cn: 想象一道影子长到横跨整条街。

examples.en: The stadium was filled with an enormous crowd.
examples.cn: 体育场里挤满了庞大的人群。

examples.en: She felt enormous relief when the test was over.
examples.cn: 考试结束后她感到极大的宽慰。

examples.en: Building the bridge took an enormous effort.
examples.cn: 修建这座桥付出了巨大的努力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一挪磨死」——一块石头要挪动会磨死人，因为它实在太大了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 e-（出于）+ norma（规则、曲尺）→ enormis（不合常规的、骇人的）→ 古法语 enorme → 中古英语 enormous，后以「巨大」为主要义项。

sensesIntro.en: Being outside the rule first described monstrous things, then huge ones, and the size sense now reaches both physical and abstract quantities.
sensesIntro.cn: 「超出常规」最初描述骇人之物，随后转向巨大之物，如今尺寸义既覆盖具体物体也覆盖抽象数量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something so large that it exceeds every normal measure.
core.cn: 核心意象：某个东西大到超越一切正常尺度。

branches.en: Physical size beyond expectation is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 超出预期的物理尺寸，是日常义项。

branches.en: Abstract quantity beyond expectation extends the same excess.
branches.cn: 超出预期的抽象数量，延伸同样的「过度」。

branches.en: The old sense of monstrous or outrageous keeps the moral origin alive.
branches.cn: 「骇人、极恶」的旧义保留了这个词的道德起源。

branches.en: Big objects and big amounts both break the normal scale.
branches.cn: 巨大物体与巨大数量都突破正常尺度。

branches.en: Excess in degree can impress or horrify, depending on context.
branches.cn: 程度上的过度既可令人惊叹，也可令人惊骇。

intro.en: Enormous is a Latin adjective built from a prefix and the noun norma, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: enormous 是由前缀与名词 norma 构成的拉丁形容词，其词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The prefix e- means out of, and norma means rule, so enormis is outside the rule.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 e- 表示出于，norma 表示规则，所以 enormis 就是「超出规则」。

items.exampleCN: e- 出现在 enormis 与 enormous 开头。

items.example: Norma is the root of enormous and norm.
items.exampleCN: norma 是 enormous 与 norm 的词根。
enormis 由 e- 与 norma 合成。

items.example: Enormous keeps the idea of exceeding measure.
items.exampleCN: enormous 保留了「超出尺度」的意思。

items.example: Enormity adds -ity to the same stem.

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词词尾

definition_zh: adv. 极其；大大地；庞大地
definition_en: to a very great degree, or on a scale so large that it exceeds the usual measure
core_image: 新铁路通车后，货运站旁的仓库一间挨着一间扩建出去
scene: 新铁路通车后，货运站旁的仓库一间挨着一间扩建出去。The freight yard grew enormously within a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 enormously 指「庞大地；巨大地」（第 2 个义项：在超出常规的规模上）；句意是十年之间货运站的面积成倍增长。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: to a degree that is very large
senses.definitionCN: （副词）在非常大的程度上
senses.example: The new route helped enormously.
senses.exampleCN: 新路线帮了极大的忙。
senses.why: A kettle emptied into a swimming pool and the water level still moves
senses.whyCN: 一壶水倒进游泳池，水面仍然看得见上涨

senses.title: On a very large scale
senses.definition: on a scale so large that it exceeds the usual measure
senses.definitionCN: （副词）在超出常规、极大的规模上
senses.example: The freight yard grew enormously within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 十年之间，货运站的规模扩充了数倍。
senses.why: A single shed rebuilt into a hall that needs two lamps to light
senses.whyCN: 一间棚屋改建成了要两盏灯才照得亮的大厅

senses.title: With spoken emphasis
senses.definition: used to strengthen an adjective or a comparative in speech
senses.definitionCN: （副词）在口语中加强形容词或比较级
senses.example: The film was enormously better than the trailer.
senses.exampleCN: 成片比预告片好得多。
senses.why: A hand waving away the plain word good until only very good remains
senses.whyCN: 一只手把平常的好字挥开，只留下非常好的

intro.en: Enormously is enormous plus -ly. Enormous carries the Latin prefix e-, away from, plus norma, a square used by a carpenter, so the word first described a shape that stepped outside the rule.
intro.cn: enormously 由 enormous 加 -ly 构成。enormous 是拉丁语 e-（离开）加 norma（木匠的角尺），所以这个词最初描述的是一种跨到尺规之外的形状。

items.en: Norma is a square tool used as a rule.
items.cn: 拉丁语 norma 指用作标准的角尺。

items.en: Enormis means outside the normal rule.
items.cn: enormis 意为超出常规规范。

items.en: Enormous enters English for a body exceeding a standard.
items.cn: 16 世纪 enormous 进入英语，指超出标准的形体。

items.en: The adverb follows, still about size.
items.cn: 副词形式随后出现，仍指体积。

items.en: The measure shifts from size to degree.
items.cn: 19 世纪衡量对象从体积转向程度。

items.en: Speech pairs it with comparatives and past participles.
items.cn: 20 世纪口语把它与比较级及过去分词搭配。

note.en: Enormously keeps the adjective enormous in front of the adverb ending -ly; hugely and immensely measure degree from other roots, while enormity keeps the older moral sense.
note.cn: enormously 在副词词尾 -ly 前保留形容词 enormous；hugely 与 immensely 从别的词根衡量程度，而 enormity 保留较早的道德含义。

normalIntro.en: Enormous plus -ly: the adverb of a word that once meant outside the rule

normal.en: Norma is a square tool, enormis steps outside it
normal.cn: norma 是角尺，enormis 是跨到尺外

normal.en: Size came first, degree came later

normal.en: Comparison uses more and most, not the suffixes
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级借助 more 与 most，而不加词尾

normal.en: Enormously popular counts people, helped enormously counts work
normal.cn: 前者数的是观众，后者数的是帮助

normal.en: The adjective enormous keeps the size, -ly turns it into a measure
normal.cn: 形容词 enormous 保留体积，加上 -ly 就变成衡量

abstract.en: A kettle emptied into a swimming pool and the water level still moves
abstract.cn: 一壶水倒进游泳池，水面仍然看得见上涨

abstract.en: A single shed rebuilt into a hall that needs two lamps to light
abstract.cn: 一间棚屋改建成了要两盏灯才照得亮的大厅

examples.en: Interest in the evening course grew enormously.
examples.cn: 夜间课程的报名量大幅增长。

examples.en: She helped enormously during the audit.
examples.cn: 她在审计期间帮了很大的忙。

examples.en: The cost was enormously larger than the estimate.
examples.cn: 实际开销比预算大得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: enormously ＝ enormous（巨大的）＋ -ly（副词词尾）＝「极其；大大地」。enormous 拆开是拉丁语 e-（离开）＋ norma（角尺、规范），本义是偏离标准、大到不合规矩，因此最早带贬义。副词两条主线：17 世纪说体积，19 世纪说程度。比较级 more enormously、最高级 most enormously。常见搭配 enormously popular、helped enormously、grateful enormously。

root: 拉丁语 norma（角尺；规范）→ 拉丁语 enormis（偏离规范、巨大的）→ enormous ＋ 副词词尾 -ly → enormously（极大地）

sensesIntro.en: Two measures and one spoken push: a yard that keeps growing, a water level that rises, an adjective needing a stronger word
sensesIntro.cn: 两种衡量加一次口语上的推动：不断扩建的场地、上涨的水位、需要更重说法的形容词

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shed rebuilt again and again until one room needs two lamps
core.cn: 核心意象：一间棚屋反复扩建，直到一个屋里要挂两盏灯

branches.en: The adverb measures degree.
branches.cn: 副词衡量的是程度。

branches.en: The adverb measures scale.
branches.cn: 副词衡量的是规模。

branches.en: The adverb strengthens another word.
branches.cn: 副词加强另一个词。

branches.en: Both descend from a shape outside the rule.
branches.cn: 两者都出自跨到规范之外的形状。

branches.en: Both keep the force of the adjective.
branches.cn: 两者都保留形容词的力度。

intro.en: Enormously is enormous plus the adverb ending -ly; the adjective carries a weakened form of Latin ex- plus norma, a square rule.
intro.cn: enormously 由 enormous 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；形容词里含拉丁语 ex- 的弱化形式与意为角尺的 norma。

latinIntro.en: Norma gave English norm, normal and enormous along three different borrowing routes, all keeping the idea of a standard.
latinIntro.cn: norma 通过三条不同的借用路径给出英语的 norm、normal 与 enormous，都保留标准之义。

definition_zh: 询问；打听；调查
definition_en: to ask for information, especially in a polite or official way
core_image: 推开办公室的门，礼貌地问一句「请问这里能报名吗」
scene: 她打电话到酒店，询问周末还有没有空房。She called the hotel to enquire about a room for the weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 enquire 是「询问；打听」（第 1 个义项：为获取信息而提问）；句意：她打电话到酒店，询问周末是否有房间。

senses.title: To ask for information
senses.definition: to ask someone for information about something
senses.definitionCN: 向某人询问某事物的信息
senses.example: I called to enquire about the train times.
senses.exampleCN: 我打电话询问火车时刻。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to seek into, so enquiring is looking into a matter by asking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「探入寻求」，所以 enquire 就是通过提问去了解一件事。

senses.title: To ask about someone's health
senses.definition: to ask how someone is, especially after illness or absence
senses.definitionCN: 询问某人近况，尤指病后或久未见面时
senses.example: She enquired after his mother at the end of the call.
senses.exampleCN: 通话结束时她问起了他母亲的身体。
senses.why: Asking for information naturally includes asking about a person's wellbeing.
senses.whyCN: 寻求信息自然包括询问一个人的状况。

senses.title: To investigate officially
senses.definition: to try to find out the facts about an event, especially officially
senses.definitionCN: 试图查明某事件的事实，尤指正式调查
senses.example: The committee will enquire into the causes of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会将调查事故原因。
senses.why: Seeking information can become a formal process, which gives the investigative sense.
senses.whyCN: 寻求信息可以发展为正式程序，于是产生「调查」义项。

intro.en: Enquire comes from Latin inquirere, to seek into, from in- and quaerere, to seek; the en- spelling comes through French.
intro.cn: enquire 来自拉丁语 inquirere（探入寻求），由 in- 与 quaerere（寻求）构成；en- 拼写经法语而来。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问或探问。

items.en: Inquirere adds in- and means to search into or investigate.
items.cn: inquirere 加上 in-，意为深入查找或调查。

items.en: Old French enquerre changes the prefix sound and carries the verb toward English.
items.cn: 古法语 enquerre 改变前缀读音，并把这个动词带向英语。

items.en: Middle English enqueren keeps both the asking and the investigating senses.
items.cn: 中古英语 enqueren 兼有询问与调查两种含义。

items.en: Enquire and inquire split as British and Latin-style spellings.
items.cn: enquire 与 inquire 分化为英式拼写和拉丁式拼写。

items.en: British English often prefers enquire for asking and inquire for formal investigation.
items.cn: 英式英语常用 enquire 表示一般询问，用 inquire 表示正式调查。

note.en: Enquire is the British spelling beside inquire, and its meaning sits with ask, question, and investigate.
note.cn: enquire 是与 inquire 并行的英式拼写，词义与 ask、question、investigate 相邻。

normalIntro.en: Enquire and inquire differ only in the first vowel, and both contain quire, the seeking sound also heard in question.
normalIntro.cn: enquire 与 inquire 只差第一个元音，两者都含 quire 这个「寻求」的音，也见于 question。

normal.en: Think of question inside enquire: to enquire is to ask a question.

normal.en: Enquire about is the pattern for asking for details.
normal.cn: enquire about 是询问细节的搭配。

normal.en: Enquire after is only for asking about a person's health.
normal.cn: enquire after 只用于问候某人的健康。

normal.en: Enquire into is the formal phrase for investigating.
normal.cn: enquire into 是表示调查的正式短语。

normal.en: British writing often uses en- for general asking and in- for official inquiries.
normal.cn: 英式写作常用 en- 表示一般询问，用 in- 表示正式调查。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised politely at an information desk.
abstract.cn: 想象在问询台前礼貌地举起一只手。

abstract.en: Imagine a phone call that begins with a careful question.
abstract.cn: 想象一通以谨慎提问开头的电话。

abstract.en: Think of a clerk opening a file to check the facts.
abstract.cn: 想象职员打开档案核对事实。

examples.en: She enquired about the price of the tickets.
examples.cn: 她询问了票价。

examples.en: He enquired after her father's health.
examples.cn: 他问起了她父亲的身体状况。

examples.en: The judge will enquire into the handling of the case.
examples.cn: 法官将调查此案的处理过程。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ quaerere（寻求）→ inquirere（深入查问）→ 古法语 enquerre → 中古英语 enquire，英式拼写保留 en-。

sensesIntro.en: Asking for information is the core, asking after a person is its social form, and enquiring into a matter is its official form.
sensesIntro.cn: 获取信息是核心，问候某人是它的社交形式，而调查某事是它的正式形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stepping toward a source of information and asking.
core.cn: 核心意象：走向信息源，开口发问。

branches.en: Asking for information is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 询问信息，是基本义项。

branches.en: Asking after someone applies the same act to a person's health.
branches.cn: 问候某人，把同一动作用于对方的健康。

branches.en: Investigating is asking in an official and sustained way.
branches.cn: 调查是以正式而持续的方式发问。

branches.en: Information about things and about people uses one verb.
branches.cn: 询问事物与问候人都用同一个动词。

branches.en: A simple question can grow into a formal inquiry.
branches.cn: 一个简单问题可以发展为正式调查。

intro.en: Enquire is a French-shaped verb built on the Latin seeking root quaerere.
intro.cn: enquire 是法语形态的动词，建立在拉丁「寻求」词根 quaerere 上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin in- means into, and quaerere means to seek, so inquirere is to seek into a matter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 in- 表示进入，quaerere 表示寻求，所以 inquirere 就是「深入查问」。

items.example: Quaerere is the root of enquire and question.

items.example: Inquirere is the Latin source of enquire.

definition_zh: 询问；打听；调查
definition_en: a question you ask to get information, or an official investigation
core_image: 一张写着问题的小纸条被递进窗口，里面的人开始翻资料
scene: 前台接到一通电话，对方仔细询问了房价和早餐时间。The enquiry was passed to the manager for a full answer.
sceneCN: 这里 enquiry 是「询问」（第 1 个义项：为获取信息而提出的问题）；句意：这个询问被转给经理，以便给出完整答复。

senses.title: A request for information
senses.definition: a question asked in order to get information
senses.definitionCN: 为获取信息而提出的问题
senses.example: We received an enquiry about the price of the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 我们收到一个询问公寓价格的电话。
senses.why: The noun names the question produced by the verb enquire.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指 enquire 这个动词所产生的「问题」。

senses.title: An official investigation
senses.definition: a formal process of finding out the facts about something
senses.definitionCN: 查明某事物事实的正式程序
senses.example: A public enquiry was opened into the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 针对这起事故启动了公开调查。
senses.why: A sustained set of questions becomes an official inquiry with its own procedure.
senses.whyCN: 持续的一连串问题会变成具有自身程序的正式调查。

senses.title: The act of asking
senses.definition: the act of asking for information rather than the question itself
senses.definitionCN: 获取信息的提问行为，而不是问题本身
senses.example: The enquiry took several days of careful checking.
senses.exampleCN: 这次询问花了好几天仔细核查。
senses.why: Like many nouns in -y, it can name the whole activity and not only its single product.
senses.whyCN: 和许多 -y 结尾的名词一样，它可指整个活动，而不只是单个产物。

intro.en: Enquiry is enquire plus the noun ending -y, from Latin inquirere, to seek into.
intro.cn: enquiry 是 enquire 加名词词尾 -y，源自拉丁语 inquirere（深入查问）。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问或探问。

items.en: Inquirere means to search into a matter.
items.cn: inquirere 意为深入查问一件事。

items.en: Old French enquerre supplies the en- form of the verb.
items.cn: 古法语 enquerre 提供动词的 en- 形式。

items.en: Middle English enqueren gives the noun enquere or enquiry.
items.cn: 中古英语 enqueren 产生名词 enquere 或 enquiry。

items.en: Enquiry is used for both polite questions and formal investigations.
items.cn: enquiry 既用于礼貌询问，也用于正式调查。

items.en: British English often keeps enquiry, while American English prefers inquiry.
items.cn: 英式英语常保留 enquiry，美式英语更常用 inquiry。

note.en: Enquiry is the noun of enquire, and it sits beside inquiry, question, and investigation.
note.cn: enquiry 是 enquire 的名词，与 inquiry、question、investigation 相邻。

abstract.en: Picture a note with three questions pushed across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一张写着三个问题的纸条被推过柜台。

abstract.en: Imagine a file labelled with a case number and filled with interviews.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标着案号、装满访谈记录的档案。

abstract.en: Think of a phone ringing at an information desk.
abstract.cn: 想象问询台的电话响起。

examples.en: She made an enquiry about the job online.
examples.cn: 她在网上询问了这份工作的情况。

examples.en: The council ordered an enquiry into the fire.
examples.cn: 议会下令调查这场火灾。

examples.en: All enquiries should be sent to the address below.
examples.cn: 所有询问请寄往下述地址。

dict_mnemonic.text: enquire（询问）+ -y（名词词尾）＝询问或调查；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: enquire（询问，源自拉丁语 inquirere「深入查问」）+ 名词词尾 -y，指提出的问题、询问行为或正式调查。

sensesIntro.en: A single question comes first, then a formal investigation, then the whole activity of asking.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是一个具体问题，再是正式调查，最后是整个询问活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a question handed over and followed until it is answered.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个问题被递出去，并一路追到有答案。

branches.en: A request for information is the basic noun sense.
branches.cn: 获取信息的请求，是基本名词义项。

branches.en: A sustained and official set of questions becomes an investigation.
branches.cn: 持续而正式的一连串问题成为调查。

branches.en: The noun can also name the activity of asking as a whole.
branches.cn: 这个名词也可指整个询问活动。

branches.en: One question and the whole process of asking share the same name.
branches.cn: 单个问题与整个询问过程共享同一名称。

branches.en: A simple enquiry can grow into a public investigation.
branches.cn: 简单询问可以发展为公开调查。

intro.en: Enquiry is a French-shaped noun built on the Latin seeking root with the English ending -y.
intro.cn: enquiry 是法语形态的名词，建立在拉丁「寻求」词根上，并加英语词尾 -y。

latinIntro.en: The Latin inquirere means to seek into, from in- and quaerere, to seek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inquirere 意为深入查问，由 in- 与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 enquiry 开头。

items.example: Quaerere is the root of enquiry.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是 enquiry 的词根。

items.example: Inquirere is the Latin source of enquiry.
items.exampleCN: inquirere 是 enquiry 的拉丁来源。

items.example: Enquire is the base of enquiry.
items.exampleCN: enquire 是 enquiry 的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

items.exampleCN: enquiry 由 enquire 与 -y 合成。
enquiries 把 enquiry 变为 -ies 复数。
enquirer 共享 enquire 词干。

definition_zh: vt. 使暴怒；激怒；使发狂
definition_en: to make someone extremely angry, or to drive an animal into a violent fury
core_image: 一句嘲讽之后，握杯的手先把杯子放下，再抬起来按住桌沿
scene: 一句嘲讽之后，握杯的手先把杯子放下，再抬起来按住桌沿。One careless remark enrages even the most patient negotiator.
sceneCN: 这里 enrages 指「使暴怒」（第 1 个义项：把人放进怒气里）；句意是一句不经心的话就能让最有耐心的谈判者当场发作。

pos.zh: 使暴怒；激怒；使（动物）发狂

senses.title: To make furiously angry
senses.definition: to make someone extremely angry
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使某人极度愤怒
senses.example: One careless remark enrages even the most patient negotiator.
senses.exampleCN: 一句不经心的话，能让最有耐心的谈判者也当场发作。
senses.why: A coffee cup set down carefully, then a hand flattening the table edge
senses.whyCN: 一只咖啡杯被小心放下，接着一只手按平桌沿

senses.title: To drive an animal to fury
senses.definition: to drive an animal into a violent fury
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使动物陷入狂暴
senses.example: The dogs barked up the slope and enraged the bull.
senses.exampleCN: 狗群沿坡狂吠，把那头公牛激得发狂。
senses.why: A bull stamping the same spot until the dust rises
senses.whyCN: 公牛在同一处反复践踏，尘土扬了起来

senses.title: To provoke on purpose
senses.definition: to provoke anger deliberately
senses.definitionCN: （动词）蓄意激起愤怒
senses.example: The last line was written to enrage the editor.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那一行就是为了让编辑发怒才写下的。
senses.why: One sentence added at the bottom of an otherwise polite letter
senses.whyCN: 一封原本客气的信，末尾多出来的一句话

intro.en: Enrage is en- plus rage. Rage reaches English through Old French from Latin rabere, to be mad, so enrage literally means to put someone inside that madness.
intro.cn: enrage 由 en- 加 rage 构成。rage 经古法语来自拉丁语 rabere（发疯），所以 enrage 的字面意思就是把某人放进那种疯狂里。

items.en: Rabere means to be mad in Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 rabere 意为发疯。

items.en: Rabies names the madness passed on by a bite.
items.cn: rabies 指由咬伤传出的疯狂。

items.en: Old French rage carries the noun into French.
items.cn: 古法语 rage 把名词带入法语。

items.en: Rage enters English for violent anger.
items.cn: 13 世纪 rage 进入英语，指暴怒。

items.en: The prefixed verb appears in English writing.
items.cn: 16 世纪带前缀的动词出现在英语书写中。

items.en: Hunting writers apply it to a cornered animal.
items.cn: 17 世纪狩猎写作者把它用于被逼入绝境的动物。

note.en: Enrage and engage differ by one letter; rage and derange share the Latin stem for madness, while infuriate and incense state the same effect from other roots.
note.cn: enrage 与 engage 只差一个字母；rage 与 derange 共用表示疯狂的拉丁词根，而 infuriate 与 incense 从别的词根说明同一种效果。

entries.definition: violent and uncontrollable anger
to disturb the order of a mind
to occupy attention or to hire
to make someone extremely angry
to make someone feel angry
to make someone very angry in formal use
to cause anger on purpose or by carelessness

normalIntro.en: En plus rage: to put anger into someone
normalIntro.cn: en- 加 rage：把怒气放进一个人身上

normal.en: Rabere is to be mad, rage is the noun it left behind
normal.cn: rabere 是发疯，rage 是它留下的名词

normal.en: En- turns the noun into an act done to someone else
normal.cn: en- 把名词变成对别人做出的动作

normal.en: A cup set down, a hand on the table, a bull in one spot
normal.cn: 一只放下的杯子、按在桌沿的手、原地踏土的公牛

normal.en: Engage and enrage differ by one letter and a great deal of heat
normal.cn: 两个词只差一个字母，火气却差一大截

normal.en: The passive reads most often: the crowd was enraged
normal.cn: 被动式最常见：人群被激怒了

abstract.en: A coffee cup set down carefully, then a hand flattening the table edge
abstract.cn: 一只咖啡杯被小心放下，接着一只手按平桌沿

abstract.en: A bull stamping the same spot until the dust rises
abstract.cn: 公牛在同一处反复践踏，尘土扬了起来

abstract.en: One sentence added at the bottom of an otherwise polite letter
abstract.cn: 一封原本客气的信，末尾多出来的一句话

examples.en: The notice enraged the tenants along the whole street.
examples.cn: 这则通知激怒了整条街的租客。

examples.en: Nothing enraged the driver more than a polite smile.
examples.cn: 没有什么比一个客气的微笑更让那名司机恼怒。

examples.en: The smell of smoke enraged the herd.
examples.cn: 烟味把牛群激得狂躁不安。

dict_mnemonic.text: enrage ＝ en-（使…进入）＋ rage（暴怒）＝「使暴怒」。rage 来自拉丁语 rabere（发疯），同源的 rabies 是狂犬病。前缀 en- 把名词变成及物动词，宾语只能是人或动物。三条线：日常语境使人发火、狩猎语境使动物发狂、写作语境指蓄意挑衅。被动 be enraged 比主动更常用，过去分词 enraged 常作表语或定语。

root: 拉丁语 rabere（发疯）→ 古法语 rage（暴怒）→ en- ＋ rage → enrage（使进入暴怒）

sensesIntro.en: Three heats of anger: a hand on the table edge, a bull in the dust, one extra sentence in a polite letter
sensesIntro.cn: 三种热度不同的怒气：按在桌沿的手、尘土里的公牛、一封客气信里多出来的一句

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup set down first, then a hand pressed flat on the table edge
core.cn: 核心意象：先把杯子放下，随后一只手按平在桌沿

branches.en: A person loses patience.
branches.cn: 一个人失去耐心。

branches.en: An animal loses control.
branches.cn: 一只动物失去控制。

branches.en: Someone plans the provocation.
branches.cn: 有人蓄意挑起。

branches.en: Both begin with words.
branches.cn: 两者都由话语引起。

branches.en: Both end in the body, not in speech.
branches.cn: 两者最后都落在身体上，而不是言语上。

intro.en: Enrage is en- plus rage; en- makes the noun transitive, and rage traces back to Latin rabere, to be mad.
intro.cn: enrage 由 en- 加 rage 构成；en- 使名词变成及物动词，rage 可追溯到拉丁语 rabere（发疯）。

latinIntro.en: Rabere gave Latin rabies and, through Old French, English rage; the same stem returns later in rabid and in derange.
latinIntro.cn: rabere 给出拉丁语 rabies，并经古法语给出英语 rage；同一词根后来在 rabid 与 derange 中再次出现。

definition_zh: vt. 使狂喜；使入迷；使全神贯注
definition_en: to fill someone with such delight that the attention is carried away from everything around
core_image: 大提琴的第一弓落下，两千人的厅堂连呼吸都放轻了
scene: 大提琴的第一弓落下，两千人的厅堂连呼吸都放轻。The opening movement enraptured a hall of two thousand.
sceneCN: 这里 enraptured 指「使（听众）入迷」（第 3 个义项：把整座厅堂的注意全部抓住）；句意是开场乐章让两千人的会场彻底安静。

pos.zh: 使狂喜；使入迷；使全神贯注

senses.title: To fill with delight
senses.definition: to fill someone with delight
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使某人充满狂喜
senses.example: The news enraptured the whole household.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让全家人都欢喜起来。
senses.why: A letter read aloud twice before anyone could speak
senses.whyCN: 一封信被大声读了两遍，才有人开口说话

senses.title: To carry the mind away
senses.definition: to carry the attention away from the room around
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把注意力从周围的房间里带走
senses.example: An old documentary enraptured a class of teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 一部老纪录片让一整班少年看得入了神。
senses.why: A student holding the same frame on the screen with a notebook still unwritten
senses.whyCN: 一个学生盯着屏幕上定住的那一格，面前的笔记本一个字也没写

senses.title: To hold an audience
senses.definition: to hold an audience so completely that it forgets itself
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把听众吸引到完全忘我的程度
senses.example: The opening movement enraptured a hall of two thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 开场乐章让两千人的大厅一片寂静。
senses.why: Two thousand people forgetting to cough between the movements
senses.whyCN: 两千人在乐章之间忘了咳嗽

intro.en: Enrapture is en- plus rapture. Rapture comes from Latin raptura, a carrying off, from rapere, to seize, so to enrapture is to take the attention of someone away.
intro.cn: enrapture 由 en- 加 rapture 构成。rapture 来自拉丁语 raptura（掳走），其动词是 rapere（抓住），所以 enrapture 就是抓住别人的注意力并把它带走。

items.en: Rapere means to seize or to carry off.
items.cn: 拉丁语 rapere 意为抓住、掳走。

items.en: Raptura names the state of being carried off.
items.cn: raptura 指被带走的状态。

items.en: Rapture enters English for the soul taken up in spirit.
items.cn: 14 世纪 rapture 进入英语，指灵魂被提升的状态。

items.en: The verb with en- appears in religious writing.
items.cn: 16 世纪带 en- 的动词出现在宗教写作中。

items.en: Reviews apply it to an audience held by music.
items.cn: 19 世纪乐评把它用于被音乐抓住的听众。

items.en: The adjective becomes common in concert reporting.
items.cn: 20 世纪形容词在音乐会报道中变得常见。

note.en: Enrapture, capture and ravish all come from Latin rapere, to seize; entrance and spellbind describe the same stillness from other roots, with the seizing image left out.
note.cn: enrapture、capture 与 ravish 都来自拉丁语 rapere（抓住）；entrance 与 spellbind 从别的词根描述同一种静止，只是省掉了抓取的意象。

entries.definition: a feeling of intense pleasure
showing extreme delight
to take something by force
to fill someone with wonder so that they cannot move
to charm or attract strongly
to hold attention completely
to give great pleasure to

normalIntro.en: En plus rapture: to put someone into carried-off delight
normalIntro.cn: en- 加 rapture：把人放进那种被掳走的欢喜里

normal.en: Rapere is to seize, rapture is the seized state
normal.cn: rapere 是抓住，rapture 是被抓住的状态

normal.en: The prefix en- makes the noun an act done to someone
normal.cn: 前缀 en- 把名词变成对某人做的动作

normal.en: A letter, a paused screen, a full hall: three degrees of attention
normal.cn: 一封信、一帧定住的画面、一座满座的厅堂：三种专注的程度

normal.en: Capture and enrapture share the same seizing root
normal.cn: capture 与 enrapture 共用同一个表示抓取的词根

normal.en: The passive reads best: the audience was enraptured
normal.cn: 被动式读起来最自然：观众听得如痴如醉

abstract.en: A letter read aloud twice before anyone could speak
abstract.cn: 一封信被大声读了两遍，才有人开口说话

abstract.en: A student holding the same frame on the screen with a notebook still unwritten
abstract.cn: 一个学生盯着屏幕上定住的那一格，面前的笔记本一个字也没写

abstract.en: Two thousand people forgetting to cough between the movements
abstract.cn: 两千人在乐章之间忘了咳嗽

examples.en: Her first two bars enraptured the judges.
examples.cn: 她开头的两小节就让评委们着了迷。

examples.en: The storyteller enraptured the children for an hour.
examples.cn: 讲故事的人让孩子们入迷地听了一个小时。

examples.en: Whole rows of readers were enraptured by the final page.
examples.cn: 最后一页让一排排读者都放不下书。

dict_mnemonic.text: enrapture ＝ en-（使…进入）＋ rapture（狂喜，本义是被掳走）＝「使狂喜；使入迷」。rapture 来自拉丁语 rapere（抓住），同族的 capture、ravish、rapturous 共用这个词根。动词的宾语可以是人、听众或读者；过去分词 enraptured 常作定语或表语，现在分词 enrapturing 修饰声音与表演。舞台与乐评语境最常用，这类写作里多用被动式。

root: 拉丁语 rapere（抓住；掳走）→ 拉丁语 raptura（被掳走的状态）→ rapture（狂喜）＋ en- → enrapture（使狂喜；使入迷）

sensesIntro.en: Three scenes of being carried off: a letter read twice, a screen held on one frame, a hall that forgets to breathe
sensesIntro.cn: 三种被带走的情景：读两遍的信、停在某一格的屏幕、忘了呼吸的满厅观众

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first bow of a cello and a full hall that stops breathing
core.cn: 核心意象：大提琴的第一弓落下，满厅的人停止了呼吸

chain: A HALL THAT FORGETS TO BREATHE

branches.en: A feeling lifts one household.
branches.cn: 一种情绪带动一家人。

branches.en: Attention leaves the room.
branches.cn: 注意力离开了房间。

branches.en: A whole audience holds still.
branches.cn: 整座听众静止不动。

branches.en: Both begin without any planning.
branches.cn: 两者都始于毫无准备。

branches.en: Both are measured by time that goes unnoticed.
branches.cn: 两者都以不知不觉过去的时间来衡量。

intro.en: Enrapture is en- plus rapture; rapture comes from Latin raptura, the state of being seized, from rapere, to seize.
intro.cn: enrapture 由 en- 加 rapture 构成；rapture 来自拉丁语 raptura（被抓住的状态），其动词是 rapere（抓住）。

latinIntro.en: Rapere gives English rapture, capture, ravish and rapturous by four different routes of borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: rapere 通过四条不同的借用路径分别给出英语的 rapture、capture、ravish 与 rapturous。
